input: Prepare me for a meeting with Monday.com (monday.com)

what_they_do.value: monday.com describes itself as "the AI work platform that not only helps manage and orchestrate work, but also does the work for you"—bringing people, workflows, and AI agents together across work management, CRM, service, and development.

priorities.priority: Make AI agents the core product and execution layer
priorities.evidence: The company says it rebuilt the platform around people and agents; native agents can plan, coordinate, and execute work under existing permissions, security, and governance.

priorities.priority: Expand the AI product surface through Sidekick, Agents, Vibe, and MCP
priorities.evidence: monday.com's 2026 AI overview identifies four additions: agents for delegated work, Sidekick for context-aware assistance, Vibe for prompt-to-app building, and MCP for connecting external AI assistants.

priorities.priority: Drive AI monetization via consumption-based pricing and AI credits
priorities.evidence: Q1 management said the company was shifting to consumption-based pricing; Q2 reported that AI-product ARR doubled from Q1 and represented 17% of net new ARR.

priorities.priority: Move further upmarket and grow larger-account adoption
priorities.evidence: Q2 results reported growth in customers above $50,000, $100,000, and $500,000 ARR, with customers above 10 users representing 82% of ARR and customers above $50,000 ARR representing 43% of ARR.

priorities.priority: Operate as a faster, flatter company with sharper product focus
priorities.evidence: Co-CEOs Roy Mann and Eran Zinman said the company restructured, sharpened its product portfolio, and committed fully to the AI Work Platform, describing the target state as faster and flatter with clearer priorities.

challenges.challenge: Organizational disruption and execution risk from the AI-led restructuring
challenges.evidence: The company disclosed that it made the difficult decision to restructure while committing fully to the AI Work Platform; its disclosed risk factors say the restructuring may not achieve expected benefits or costs may exceed expectations.

challenges.challenge: Managing the scope and complexity of a rapidly grown, multi-product business
challenges.evidence: The Q2 release lists as a risk the company's ability to effectively manage the scope and complexity of its business following years of rapid growth.

challenges.challenge: Reducing dependence on monday work management while broadening adoption of newer products
challenges.evidence: The company's disclosed risk factors say it continues to derive a majority of revenue from monday work management, while its strategy is expanding across CRM, service, dev, and AI products.

challenges.challenge: AI, security, privacy, interoperability, and regulatory exposure as agents take action
challenges.evidence: The Q2 release explicitly lists risks related to AI and machine learning, security incidents, privacy and cross-border data restrictions, new AI regulation, and the ability of the platform to interoperate with software applications.

recent_changes.headline: monday.com scheduled its Q3 2026 results announcement
recent_changes.summary: The company announced that it would report third-quarter 2026 financial results, indicating an upcoming investor checkpoint during the current AI-platform transition.

recent_changes.headline: monday.com detailed its 2026 AI Workspace capabilities
recent_changes.summary: The company published an overview of Sidekick, Agents, Vibe, and MCP, positioning AI as an execution layer across departments rather than a standalone assistant.

recent_changes.headline: monday.com reported Q2 2026 results and emphasized its AI-platform reset
recent_changes.summary: Q2 revenue was reported at $364.6 million, up 22% year over year; management said AI-product ARR doubled from Q1 and that the organization was being restructured around a faster, flatter AI Work Platform company.

key_people.name: Roy Mann
key_people.title: Co-Founder & Co-CEO
key_people.recent: In the May AI-platform launch, he said monday.com was shifting from helping teams manage work to being a place where people and agents work side by side.

key_people.name: Eran Zinman
key_people.title: Co-Founder & Co-CEO
key_people.recent: In the May launch, he called the AI Work Platform the biggest change in company history and said monday.com owed its 250,000 customers a platform built for what comes next.

key_people.name: Daniel Lereya
key_people.title: Chief Product and Technology Officer
key_people.recent: The management page says he leads global R&D and Product teams on product strategy, vision, and execution—directly relevant to the AI-platform rebuild.

key_people.name: Adi Dar
key_people.title: Chief Customer Officer
key_people.recent: He is responsible for end-to-end customer ownership, including adoption, retention, and customer satisfaction, and oversees non-sales customer-facing teams.

key_people.name: Casey George
key_people.title: Chief Revenue Officer
key_people.recent: He leads revenue and previously held global sales leadership roles at Qlik and Talend, making him relevant to enterprise expansion and AI monetization discussions.

talking_points: Which AI-agent use cases are converting fastest from pilot to paid, and what proof of ROI is required for enterprise expansion?
As the company becomes faster and flatter, where are implementation, governance, or change-management bottlenecks showing up for customers and internal teams?
How is monday.com balancing agent autonomy with permissions, security, privacy, and human approval as agents begin executing cross-department work?
